item.title: COMING THURSDAY SEPTEMER 3rd |The Movement & Pepper w/sg Surfer Girl — Mon Aug 31 — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
Thursday, September 3 • 5:00 pm – 10:00 pm | From $61.33 Event Details and Tickets Come join us for a night of live music on the outdoor stage as part of the French Broad River Brewery Summer Concert Series! The Movement: The Movement has been winning the hearts and minds of alt-reggae fans since their inception in 2003.Drawing inspiration from Sublime, 311, Slightly Stoopid, and John Brown’s Body, they’ve made a name for themselves as reggae shapeshifters with a foundation of insightful lyrics and heavy drum and bass.
“Kona Dub-Rock.” That’s how Pepper describes their blend of reggae, alternative rock, dub, island rhythms, and punk rock energy. It’s a sound that’s taken the trio from the Big Island of Hawaii — where vocalist/guitarist Kaleo Wassman, vocalist/bassist Bret Bollinger, and drummer Yesod Williams held their first band practice as teenagers in the late 1990s — to the upper reaches of Billboard’s Reggae Albums chart, where 2019’s Local Motion peaked at Number 1.

item.description:
Boomtown Arts & Heritage FestAVL proudly announces its return for a third year, set for September 4 – 6, 2026, at Pack Square Park in the heart of downtown Asheville. The free, all-ages festival celebrates Western North Carolina’s local music, regional culture, and architectural history with multi-genre main stage performances, interactive family programming, and heritage trail tours. FESTIVAL SCHEDULE – ALL FREE WITH RSVP

item.description: Join Alex Bazemore and Friends for a Monday night residency at French Broad River Brewery. The bluegrass/ Jamgrass group is a mash up of local Asheville “all star” musicians set to explore new musical frontiers together and melt faces. Alex and his rotating cast of local musicians play sets with ranging genres and styles influenced by everything from bluegrass to folk, jam , funk, and blues. Free show, pet and family friendly! French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. Just minutes from the Biltmore Estate & Downtown, our taproom is a gathering spot for locals and visitors alike. We regularly host live music and entertainment in our taproom, making French Broad River Brewery a lively hub of local activity. From bluegrass to reggae, there’s always something happening. item.title: Monthly Dharma Group (Saturdays) – Meditation — Thu Sep 3, 10:30 PM
item.description:
Awakening Asheville You do not have to walk this path alone. In fact, this journey is that much more rich and enjoyable when traversed with others. Groups Openings
First Saturday of each month – mornings at 10:30 am Eastern Led by Buddhist teacher Ronya Banks, this group meets once a month, for an hour and a half.
Group Meeting Includes: Group Discussion and Sharing Instruction on Dharma/Buddhist Principles Guided Meditation Meditation Instruction Connecting with Other Practitioners Most people on a spiritual journey find it supportive, often even necessary to get the regular support of a meditation teacher, as well as the mutuality and connection with other meditation practitioners on this path.
This monthly group affords you with the opportunity to connect with a teacher and other like-minded people, wherein you will all boldly delve deeply into different ways of approaching your formal and informal mindfulness practices through the lens of the Buddhist teachings.
Price: By Donat

item.description:
Asheville Social Club # **🌇 Rooftop Meetup — Sunset at Pillar**
Let’s do another rooftop event before fall rolls in and the leafers arrive!
For this Rooftop Meetup, we’re heading to Pillar Rooftop Bar (on top of the Hilton Garden Inn) to catch the sunset, enjoy some live music, grab a drink, and spend a few hours hanging out with good people. Come for the views, stay for the conversation, or just stop by for a bit. No pressure and no complicated itinerary required.
**What to expect** · Meet up at Pillar before sunset · Live music from a band TBD, probably classic rock or island/tiki favorites · Cocktails, mocktails, or whatever you feel like having · Catch up with familiar faces and meet some new ones · Enjoy the rooftop views and hopefully spectacular Asheville sunset · Stay for 20 minutes or hang out all evening; come and go as you please

item.title: Fiber Friends — Sat Sep 5, 10:00 AM — 23 Ed Parlor
item.description:
UU Asheville Fiber Friends is a group of crafters who do handwork on personal projects and for the community. Mainly knitters and crocheters, we create warm items for donation to local charities (serving children, youth, and adults) and make a variety of cotton cloths given to Meals on Wheels for their “Santa for seniors” packages each December. A limited supply of yarn and tools (needles and hooks) are also available.
Join us the first Saturday of each month in the parlor of 23 Edwin, from 10 AM until about 12 noon. For more information or to be added to the monthly email reminder list, contact Mara Sprain.
Source: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Asheville

item.title: Tea & Tarot for the Collective — Sat Sep 5, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Awakening Asheville Tarot readings are a powerful tool for tapping into the energies that surround us and exploring the depths of our psyche.
Experience an energetic vibe check as the cards illuminate pathways to understanding, clarity, and personal growth. We'll dive into the layers of our conscious, subconscious, and unconscious beings.
Marian will do a reading for the collective group first, then dive into mini-readings for each individual in attendance.
We will have local, organic, hot herbal tea from Appalachian DiviniTEA and water available to sip on during this event.
Suggested Exchange: $10
This event is hosted by Marian Noble of Energetic Experiences. She offers [private tarot readings](https://energeticexperiences.co/tarot) in person, online, and by phone.
Source: Awakening Asheville

item.description:
Join us for a live performance by Steve Lapointe, pianist-in-residence in the Windgate Foundation Atrium. ABOUT THE MUSICIAN Steve Lapointe’s nine years of classical piano as a youth grounded him in music theory. Jazz studies while in Ithaca, New York, opened his ears to extemporaneous improvisation and the music of Keith Jarrett, Chick Corea, Bill Evans, Michel Petrucciani and the American songbook. Steve served as musical director of the Unitarian Universalist (UU) Fellowship of Vero Beach, Florida, and occasionally performed at the UU Asheville congregation. RESERVE TICKETS NOW

item.title: Men's Breakfast Discussion Group — Sat Sep 12, 8:00 AM — 23 Ed Board
item.description:
The Men’s Breakfast Discussion Group (Men’s Breakfast for short) welcomes all men to join us the second Saturday of each month for a potluck breakfast followed by group discussion on a reflective topping chosen by our members. The Breakfast begins at 8 AM, followed by our discussion from 9 to 11 AM. If you cannot attend the discussion in person, you are welcomed to join us via Zoom. We continue to meet during the summer months. Contact Carroll Canipe at canipecarroll@gmail.com for more information and Charlie St. Clair at charlie42stclair@gmail.com for information and the Zoom link.
